record.context_brief: Specific packing problem in parallelograms and prisms
record.original_question: What is the maximum number of interior points that can be placed in a parallelogram with angle pi/3 so that every pair of points is at distance at least 1, and what is the analogous maximum for the corresponding prism whose faces are such parallelograms?

evidence.quote: Find the maximum number of interior points inside of a parallelogram having an angle of pi/3 such that the distance between any two points is greater than or equal to 1. artifact.category_tag: point packing in planar and prismatic regions
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let P be a (closed) parallelogram in the Euclidean plane with side lengths a and b and one interior angle equal to π/3. Determine, as a function of a and b, the maximum number n_max(a,b) of points that can be placed in the interior of P such that any two of the chosen points are at Euclidean distance at least 1 from one another.

Analogously, let Q be the right prism whose two parallel (congruent) faces are parallelograms of side lengths a and b with an interior angle π/3, and whose height is c. Determine the maximum number N_max(a,b,c) of points that can be placed in the interior of Q so that any two of the chosen points are at Euclidean distance at least 1.

Provide explicit formulas for n_max(a,b) and N_max(a,b,c), together with optimal configurations achieving these maxima.
artifact.status_search_result: This is a classical packing exercise of the type encountered in olympiad problem collections; the parsed source indicates that explicit closed-form answers for both the parallelogram and prism cases were given as solutions. No active research literature treats this exact configuration as an open problem, so it is best regarded as solved at the level of an exercise.

status_evidence.title: arXiv math/0010143
status_evidence.snippet: Problem collection including a parallelogram packing problem with angle π/3 and its prism analogue, presented with solutions.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is presented together with explicit solutions for both the planar and prism cases.
